## What I did

The tests were already passing — per `.docs/instructions.md`, this is a refactoring exercise: the original code worked but was written as a single character-by-character loop with cryptic state (`he`, `listOpened`, `list`, and a `header == 7` special case). I rewrote `markdown.go` as a line-based parser:

- **`Render`** splits the input on newlines and classifies each line as one of three things: a header, a list item, or paragraph text. Two booleans (`inList`, `inParagraph`) track open blocks, and blocks are closed as soon as the content type changes.
- **`headerLevel`** — 1–6 leading `#` followed by a space is a header; 7+ `#` falls through to paragraph text (the old `header == 7` hack is now an explicit rule).
- **`applyEmphasis`** — extracts the inline `__bold__` / `_italic_` conversion that the original did as a pre-pass over the whole document, now applied per line (which also makes it safe: `#` and `*` inside text are never interpreted, matching the "symbols should not be interpreted" test cases).
- **`closeList` / `closeParagraph`** — small helpers that emit the closing tags, replacing the tangled end-of-input `switch` in the original.

Refactoring notes are included as comments per the spec. `markdown_test.go` and `cases_test.go` are untouched, and no new files were created.
